text: Attempt 3: compact bands again, plus un-zoned power columns next to every cross street (x=77,85,93,101), cross streets every 8 tiles, pumps wired with their own line, services and rail on a schedule, at most 5 loans.
Day one: $10,000 bond, tax 4%, avenue + neighbor link, 6 streets, 4 cross streets, power columns, bands of homes/shops/factories, coal plant, 12 pumps, pipes.
Power columns weren't linked to each other (only x=101 touched the plant). Linked them with a line along y=56; every column and pump now powered.
South pipe rows weren't connected to the pumps; added a north-south pipe at x=74.
Second bond. Block 2 south (y56-90) with its own power columns, a second coal plant (x102-105, y70-73), pipes with a north-south main at x=74, and 11 more riverbank pumps.
Tax 4% -> 6%. Factories in block 2's empty middle bands (shops were oversupplied); 11 more pumps on the x=73 power line.
Third bond. Fire station (x86-88) and police (x94-96) at y42-44. Block 3 east (x109-126, y20-55): power columns x=109/117/125 linked on y=56, homes and factory bands, pipes.
16 pumps at the river bend wired with their own power line row (y=46): all 50 pumps powered.
Fourth bond. Third coal plant by the river (x64-67, y57-60), school and hospital (y45-47), second wired pump field (27 pumps).
Block 3 south (x109-126, y56-90): streets, power columns, homes and factory bands, pipes.
Tax 6% -> 8%: loan payments ($1,400) were above tax income ($1,202). Home demand is maxed, so the higher tax should not hurt much.
